szoveg_eredeti:
AAEON BOXER-8741AI is an industrial edge AI box PC built around the NVIDIA Jetson Thor T5000 module, delivering up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS (sparse) of AI performance and featuring 128GB LPDDR5X memory.

Designed for humanoid robotics, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and multi-sensor perception workloads, it features two 10GbE and four 5GbE ports, two CAN FD interfaces, RS-232/RS-485, optional GPIO, and four USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports. Expansion options include M.2 slots for NVMe storage, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, and 4G/5G cellular connectivity. The computer supports 19V to 48V DC input and operates from -20°C to 60°C for industrial applications.

AAEON BOXER-8741AI front panel with dual 10GbE, HDMI, four USB 3.2 ports, and power input BOXER-8741AI rear panel with four 5GbE ports, COM, CAN FD, and optional DIO

On the software side, this box PC supports NVIDIA JetPack 7.1 or later, which provides access to CUDA, TensorRT, and other NVIDIA tools for AI development. It can also use NVIDIA Isaac for robotics, Metropolis for video analytics, and Holoscan for sensor processing. The device can run vision-language models (VLMs), vision-language-action (VLA) models, and other AI applications locally.

We previously wrote about AAEON’s BOXER-8742AI, which uses the lower-end Jetson T4000 module with a 12-core CPU, 64GB LPDDR5X memory, and up to 1200 FP4 TFLOPS. That model was designed for camera-related applications with its four Gigabit Ethernet PoE ports, whereas the BOXER-8741AI has more processing power and six multi-gigabit Ethernet connections. Other Jetson T5000-based industrial computers include the Lanner EAI-I351 with a 100GbE QSFP28 connector and eight GMSL2 camera inputs, and the Firefly EC-ThorT5000 with four 10GbE ports and eight GMSL2 camera interfaces.

You can purchase the AAEON BOXER-8741AI directly from the company’s online store for $10,219. At the time of writing, it’s open for preorders, and availability is expected around December 29, 2026. The listed configuration (BOXER-8741AI-JP710N-A1-1010) includes a 128GB NVMe SSD, while the 240W power adapter and power cord are sold separately. More information is available on the product page and in the press release.
